title: How the McPRIAN, Salinas Pliego and Others Profited from Carlos Manzo.
author: Mariana Álvarez Torres
content:
_This article by[Mariana Álvarez
Torres](https://www.sinembargo.mx/author/mariana-alvarez-torres/) originally
appeared in the [October 31, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4896875/como-el-mcprian-salinas-pliego-
y-otros-lucraron-con-carlos-manzo-un-ano-en-videos/), an independent Mexican
digital news outlet._

**Mexico City, October 31 (SinEmbargo).–** The **murder** of [**Carlos
Manzo**](https://www.sinembargo.mx/tag/carlos-manzo/), independent Mayor of
Uruapan, Michoacán, has been used by the opposition to drive an offensive
against the Government of President **Claudia Sheinbaum** and to promote what
was at the time presented as a spontaneous movement of **Generation Z**.

One year after the crime, that call to action, which brought together
promoters of the **Pink Tide** (Marea Rosa) and figures from the PAN and the
**right** , is widely criticized, while the [**Sombrero
Movement**](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4888820/la-fiscalia-de-michoacan-
descarta-motivos-politicos-en-el-asesinato-de-carlos-manzo/), founded by the
former mayor, is going through an internal rupture over accusations about the
handling of the investigation and the electoral aspirations of **Grecia
Quiroz** , his widow and the current Mayor.

Carlos Manzo was murdered on **November 1, 2025** during the Festival of
Candles, in the Historic Center of [Uruapan](https://uruapan.gob.mx/). The
attack took place in front of attendees and was recorded in videos that
circulated widely on social media. By that time, the former mayor had built a
public image characterized by confrontation with **criminal groups** and his
constant demands for greater support from the state and federal governments to
confront insecurity in the municipality.

Just two days after the homicide, figures from the [PAN](https://pan.org.mx/)
and the far right began to react on social media and to use the crime to
question the federal Government and its security cabinet. Thus, the Mayor's
death became one of the opposition's main arguments to denounce the situation
of violence and to call for mobilizations against the president.

Amid the first national reactions, the political exploitation of the tragedy
and the attempts to turn the murder into a partisan banner were questioned.
Manzo had won the Mayor's office of Uruapan as an independent in 2024, after
splitting from Morena, but his trajectory and political positions did not
necessarily correspond to the image that sectors of the opposition began to
build after his death.

For this reason, his brother Juan Manzo, Undersecretary of Government of
Michoacán, lamented that different groups sought to appropriate his figure to
advance their own interests. In that context, the official recalled that
Carlos had an affinity with the leftist grassroots and questioned the use of
his murder to attack the federal Government.

## Generation Z and the Pink Tide

On November 15, 2025, Mexico City (CdMx) was the scene of a mobilization
called under the name Generation Z, which used youth symbols, among them the
flag from the anime _One Piece_ , and presented itself as a nonpartisan
expression of discontent against the federal Government.

However, among the attendees there were also members of the Pink Tide, that
is, people linked to the opposition and former officials who had participated
in other mobilizations against Morena. The call brought together sectors with
different demands and positions, from young people who rejected the entire
political class to adults who focused their complaints on the Sheinbaum
Administration.

The presence of these groups called into question the spontaneous and
exclusively youthful character of the protest. Above all, the Pink Tide, which
had backed Xóchitl Gálvez during the 2024 presidential elections, reappeared
in a mobilization that sought to present itself as a citizen expression
independent of the parties.

The march ended with clashes and disturbances in the downtown area of the
capital. After the events, the presence of pro-life groups, operatives linked
to the Cuauhtémoc borough government and protesters carrying signs in English
calling for United States intervention was also documented.

After what happened, questions were directed at the organizers and the
profiles that drove the call from outside the contingents. Among the names
pointed to in the public discussion were Ricardo Salinas Pliego, Claudio X.
González and Vicente Fox, who figured in the strategy of amplifying messages
against the federal Government.

It is worth noting that the mobilization exposed great contradictions, given
that while some young people insisted that their protest did not belong to any
party, other participants defended positions and slogans linked to traditional
sectors of the opposition.

In June 2026, an investigation into far-right digital networks, carried out by
_SinEmbargo_ , exposed mechanisms of artificial amplification through _bots_
and fake accounts to position political causes, messages and calls to action.

The amplification of messages against the federal Government allowed Manzo's
murder to transcend the local sphere and become a recurring argument of the
opposition. However, the Generation Z call did not maintain the same public
presence it had during November 2025, when the Mayor's death was one of the
main triggers of the protests.

## The Sombrero Movement Fractures

While the opposition mobilization was losing strength, the Sombrero Movement
began to face an internal dispute over Carlos Manzo's legacy and the course of
the investigations into his murder.

On August 4, 2026, Juan Manzo accused members of the movement and Grecia
Quiroz of politically using his brother's death. In an interview conducted by
_SinEmbargo_ , the Undersecretary questioned why the priority was not to
clarify the homicide and pointed out that the Mayor had information that could
contribute to the investigations.

> "It is more profitable for them not to deliver results so they can
> politicize the absence of results. And it seems to me that in the case of
> the Sombrero Movement they have used Carlos's case, who is ultimately the
> one most aggrieved by this unfortunate event, so that his death becomes a
> political discourse," he stated.

One of the main points of confrontation has been the handover of Carlos
Manzo's cell phones, since his brother believes the devices could contain
relevant information about the threats he allegedly received before being
murdered.

At the same time, Juan Manzo questioned the lack of support for the arrest of
José Manuel Jiménez Miranda, identified as the former mayor's Chief of
Security and of bodyguards, as well as the defense of other members of his
inner circle who face proceedings related to the crime.

Later, on August 25, the official made public a letter addressed to Jorge
Álvarez Máynez, national leader of Movimiento Ciudadano, after that party
expressed its support for Grecia Quiroz. In the document, he accused the
political actors who took up the case of seeking votes and power from the
family tragedy. He wrote:

> You and your movement are just a few more on the long list of people for
> whom justice is the last thing they seek, but rather votes and consequently
> power and money.
>
> Juan Manzo, in a letter to Jorge Álvarez Máynez

In the letter he also pointed out that members of the Sombrero Movement and
people close to the Mayor had evidence that could help clarify the murder, but
that, according to him, they failed to hand it over to the authorities.

Two days later, Carlos Manzo's former private secretary, Jessica Yesenia
Méndez, laid out allegations about internal omissions and the relationships of
people in the municipal environment with the former mayor's team. Among the
issues addressed were the alleged leaks of information about Manzo's schedule
that would have facilitated the criminal operation.

Juan Manzo also went to Mexico City to request that the Attorney General's
Office (FGR) take over the investigation and review the possible
responsibility of people close to the former mayor.

## Grecia Quiroz Seeks the Governorship

Grecia Quiroz took over as Municipal President of Uruapan after her husband's
murder and later confirmed that she will seek the governorship of Michoacán in
2027, backed by the Sombrero Movement.

The Mayor registered the trademarks "Carlos Manzo" and "Movimiento
Independiente del Sombrero" with the Mexican Institute of Industrial Property
(IMPI), which since early 2026 she can use to organize meetings, consultations
and political activities.

Since taking office, Quiroz has held state and federal authorities responsible
for the lack of security that, she maintains, her husband faced before being
murdered. She has also demanded that the FGR take over the case to guarantee
impartiality and to dig deeper into the lines of investigation she considers
pending.

However, she has rejected Juan Manzo's claims about an alleged lack of
cooperation with the authorities. Regarding the former mayor's cell phones,
she asserted that they are available for the proceedings, as long as the
review is carried out in her presence. She also denied that the City Council
pays the fees of the lawyers of the detained bodyguards.

Juan Manzo has maintained that the priority must be to clarify the homicide
and not turn it into a tool for electoral profit. In addition, he has warned
that belonging to the Sombrero Movement must not become a means of avoiding
criminal responsibility.

> "Being part of the Sombrero Movement can become an element of impunity for
> the very crime against Carlos Manzo, and I will not accept that. Nor if
> there is impunity on the part of someone from Morena or another party," he
> told _SinEmbargo_.

## 33 Arrested and 90 Percent Progress

One year after the murder, the [Michoacán State Attorney General's Office
(FGE)](https://comunicacion.fiscaliamichoacan.gob.mx/articulos/20261028-20632026-fge-
reporta-avances-de-hasta-92-por-ciento-en-investigaciones-por-homicidios-de-
alto-impacto-social-suman-cerca-de-50-detenidos) reported 33 people arrested
and 90 percent progress in the homicide investigation, and also confirmed that
the crime was revenge by the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) for the
confrontation Carlos Manzo had with that organization.

According to the investigations, the reprisal would have originated after the
capture, on August 27, 2025, of René Belmontes Aguilar, alias "El Rhino" or
"El Chamuco," identified as the CJNG plaza boss in Uruapan. After his arrest,
Manzo exhibited and insulted him during a live broadcast on Facebook, which he
deleted minutes later.

Among those arrested are Ramón Ángel Álvarez Ayala, alias "El R1," identified
by the authorities as the leader of "Los Rs," one of the main CJNG cells in
Michoacán, and Jorge Armando Gómez Sánchez, known as "El Licenciado" or "El
Contador," accused of coordinating the attack. The Attorney General's Office
identifies them as the probable masterminds of the crime. At least 29 of those
arrested have already been ordered to stand trial.

The investigations point to an operation that would have involved prior
surveillance, leaking of information and coordination among different
participants to carry out the Mayor's murder. Among the people accused of
providing data about his movements is Samuel García Rivero, former Director of
Protocol of the City Council, accused of leaking his schedule to the criminal
cell.

On October 29, the arrest of Rosa Alejandra "N," former Well-Being Secretary
of the Uruapan City Council, was also reported; she is accused of alleged
cover-up by favoring. The official was close to the team of Carlos Manzo and
Grecia Quiroz, and is also the mother of Alejandro "N," alias "El Macas," one
of the bodyguards arrested for his alleged connection to the case.

The FGE reported that the investigation totals 3,500 actions, the analysis of
1,200 hours of video, 120 hearings, 3,000 forensic procedures and 72
information extractions. To conclude the proceedings at the state level, the
office said it still needs to obtain Manzo's two cell phones, which remain in
Grecia Quiroz's possession.

![Ramón Ángel "N", alias "El R1", identified as the alleged mastermind of the
murder of Carlos Manzo](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/11/2026-11-01-manzo-opposition-profited-el-r1.jpg)"El R1"
is identified as the main leader of "Los Rs," one of the most violent criminal
cells linked to the CJNG. Photo: SSPC

The progress in the investigation comes after months of allegations about the
participation of people close to the former mayor, the conduct of his security
team and the possible leaks that would have facilitated the attack.
Nevertheless, the political accusations against Grecia Quiroz and other
members of the Sombrero Movement do not amount to proven criminal
responsibility.

Thus, one year after the homicide, the case of Carlos Manzo remains a dispute
over justice and also over his political legacy. While the Attorney General's
Office maintains that the crime was a CJNG reprisal for the Mayor's
confrontation with that organization, the differences between his family and
the Sombrero Movement keep open the dispute over cooperation with the
authorities and the course the investigation should take.
